title: 医疗器械安全事件根本原因分析（RCA）

sources.title: InfuTronix, LLC Recalls Nimbus and Nimbus II Infusion Pump Systems for Multiple Device Failures That May Cause Severe Injury and Death | FDA
sources.key_facts: Class I recall, 52,328 units, 3,698 complaints, 6 serious injuries, 1 death, failure modes: battery failure/occlusion/system errors/drug leakage/flow rate deviation/damaged housing, FDA announcement 2024-04-25, support cutoff 2024-06-20

sources.title: Infutronix infusion pump recall linked to 6 injuries, 1 death | MedTech Dive
sources.key_facts: Distribution dates 2015-2024, February 2024 recall initiation, April 26 2024 FDA notice, 52,000+ units, lack of sterile barrier enabling microbial contamination identified as separate failure mode, potential harms: seizures/shock/organ failure/death

sources.title: InfuTronix Recalls 52,328 Infusion Pump Systems Due to Multiple Potential Failure Modes | HPN Online
sources.key_facts: 52,328 exact unit count confirmed, UDI 00817170020000 for Nimbus main pump, affected models: Nimbus Administration Set/Flex/PainPro (Halo), Nimbus II PainPRO/Flex/Plus/EpiD/EMS

sources.title: FDA says InfuTronix infusion pump recall includes 1 death | Drug Delivery Business
sources.key_facts: 1 death confirmed, 6 serious injuries, 3,698 complaints, support deadline June 20 2024, Class I classification confirmed, devices require complete redesign and new 510(k) clearance

sources.title: FDA Recall: Software anomalies can cause serious harm or death - SoftwareCPR
sources.key_facts: Recall number Z-0885-2026 confirmed, product code LVP-SW-0005, 30 units (software correction kits), affected software version 5.10.1 and earlier, distribution states: CA/CO/FL/GA/ID/IL/MD/MI/MN/MS/NE/NJ/NV/OK/OR/SC/TX/VA/WA/WI, enforcement report date 2025-12-16

sources.title: REGULATORY UPDATE: Class I Recall Issued for Fresenius Kabi Ivenix Large Volume Pump Software | AABB
sources.key_facts: Anomaly 1: battery inaccurate reporting causing unexpected shutdown; Anomaly 2: two leading zeros rate entry freezes interface; fix versions: IMS 5.2.2 + LVP 5.10.2; battery replacement threshold 70% health; customer notification November 14 (2025); 2 serious injuries no deaths as of Nov 18 2025

sources.title: FDA Class I recall: Fresenius Kabi issues urgent software correction for Ivenix infusion pumps | Manufacturing Chemist
sources.key_facts: Software version 5.10.1 and earlier (Product Code: LVP-SW-0005), two anomalies confirmed with technical detail, required update to v5.10.2, IMS update to v5.2.2, 2 serious injuries no deaths as of November 18 2025

sources.title: Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) Database | FDA
sources.key_facts: Official FDA MAUDE adverse event database, searchable by device name/manufacturer/MDR number/date, contains 10 years of MDR submissions from manufacturers/importers/user facilities/voluntary reporters

sources.title: A Hazard Analysis of Class I Recalls of Infusion Pumps | PMC
sources.key_facts: 70 Class I recalls analyzed; energy hazards 67% (47/70); device component failure 89% (64/72); hardware 69% (45/65); software 26% (17/65); underdose outcomes 55% (36/66); overdose 27% (18/66); alarm failures 15 instances; power failures 9 instances

sources.title: eCFR :: 21 CFR Part 803 -- Medical Device Reporting | Electronic Code of Federal Regulations
sources.key_facts: 21 CFR 803.50(a)(1): manufacturers must report within 30 calendar days of awareness of reportable death/serious injury; 21 CFR 803.53: 5-work-day expedited reporting for events requiring remedial action or FDA-requested reports; 21 CFR 806.10: correction/removal report within 10 working days

sources.title: FDA grades new Medtronic SynchroMed II recall as Class I event | MedTech Dive
sources.key_facts: 2019 Class I recall (legacy/red-herring case), models 8637-20 and 8637-40, 11,299 units, foreign particle causing motor stall preventing drug delivery, 5 motor stall reports, no deaths, last affected unit manufactured April 2019, Medtronic did not recommend removal of implanted devices
